reason: Both conversations give the correct and essential safety answer in one turn: stop using the cracked hob now, spills can reach live parts and cause shock or short circuit, and an engineer must replace the glass top. Both equally miss the same key step of telling her to isolate the hob at the cooker switch, and neither raises the model number or a home-insurance accidental damage claim. Conversation 1 adds a useful 'don't try to repair the crack yourself' warning while Conversation 2 adds the practical note that the whole unit may need replacing if the top isn't sold separately; these small advantages cancel out.
